fixes.explanation: That's the one, friend. The people had been saying, “All who do evil are good in the sight of the LORD, and in them He delights…” The verse opens with, “You have wearied the LORD with your words…” (Malachi 2:17). Those words are what wearied Him.
No king in this verse, friend. The LORD of Hosts says, “Behold, I will send My messenger…” That's who is coming. And the next line says what he does: he “…will prepare the way before Me.”
Yes, friend. The verse says the Lord whom they seek “…will suddenly come to His temple…” The word the text uses is suddenly. It's like pulling a drawer open and finding the light already pouring in.
The verse says the opposite, baker. The Lord whom they seek “…will suddenly come to His temple…” The word is suddenly. So the statement is true, and that one word is the one to hold onto.

Look again, friend, because this one sneaks up on you. The LORD of Hosts calls Him “…the Messenger of the covenant, in whom you delight…” So the statement is true. That delight is right there in the same breath as “…see, He is coming…” Even I had to read that line twice, and I was the one who underlined it.

No army in this verse, friend. The reason given is, “For He will be like a refiner’s fire, like a launderer’s soap.” The picture is a workshop kind of picture, not a battlefield. It's still serious enough that the verse asks, “And who can stand when He appears?”

Levi it is, baker. The verse says, “He will purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and silver.” Gold and silver are the picture here. And the verse says He will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver.

Benjamin isn't named in the verse, friend. The text says the Lord “…will purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and silver.” Levi is the name that fills the blank. Benjamin and I will both have to wait outside this one.

The verse says it plainly, friend. After the refining, “Then they will present offerings to the LORD in righteousness.” So the statement is true. I once stamped a whole batch with a dusty stamper and learned this lesson the crumbly way: clean first, then offer.
